english.title: Falsely represent that consent given or section 1 does not apply to activity - Human Tissue Act 2004
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing or believing that a person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), was going to or might do an activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTIVITY..), to which

(A)_[section 1(1)]_
(B)_[section 1(2)]_
(C)_[section 1(3)]_

of the Human Tissue Act 2004 applied, falsely represented to that person that

(D)_[there was appropriate consent to the doing of the activity]_
(E)_[the activity was not one to which the subsection applied]_

and you knew that that representation was false or did not believe it was true
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(2) and (7) of the Human Tissue Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing / believing that a person was going to/might do

falsely represented to that person

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i)Section 5(8) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides that appropriate consent has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Act.
(ii)Section 2 and 3 of the Act provide the interpretation of appropriate consent in relation to children and adults.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
